newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican police probed in death of drug trafficker.
newsitem.headline: Mexican police probed in death of drug trafficker.

text.p: Sixteen Mexican police officers are being investigated for the murder of a suspected drug trafficker known as "The Genius," government news agency Notimex reported on Thursday.
Suspected drug criminal Juan Eugenio Rosales, also known as "The Genius," was murdered earlier this month in the border city Ciudad Juarez, just across from El Paso, Texas.
The agents under investigation are Judicial Police from the state of Sonora based in Ciudad Juarez, the report said.

"Internal affairs will investigate the presence of the 16 agents in relation to the events on June 19 to clear up doubts regarding their behaviour and charges from the widow," Chihuahua state police commander Julian Calderon told the news agency.
The murder of "The Genius" is part of a wave of drug-related violence that has erupted in Mexico following the death of leading drug lord Amado Carrillo Fuentes on July 4.

On Thursday, two men were gunned down in the border town San Luis Rio Colorado, another recent hotbed of drug violence across the frontier from Arizona, Notimex reported. One victim died and the other was taken to hospital.
Citing a news release from local officials, Notimex reported that two suspects in the killings have ties to the drug trade.
On Tuesday, a former beauty queen recently identified as a liaison between drug barons and high-ranking army officers was slain in a gangland-style hit in the western city Guadalajara.
Since the death of Carrillo Fuentes, authorities have been cracking down on allegedly corrupt army officers and police agents believed linked to drug trafficking.
According to U.S. estimates, drug cartels spend $6 billion a year bribing Mexican officials for safe passage of their illicit products.
